introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Economics 2 (0525), ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2023. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: You are required to answer ANY FIVE questions. ONLY THE FIRST FIVE QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED. All questions carry equal marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown:
"LIFELESS LTD" is a company producing and selling funeral materials and it is owned by NGEME'S Family. To raise additional capital in 20XX, the company decide to sell the following securities to members.

200 preference shares at 5000 FRS per share,

400 ordinary shares at 10000 FRS per share, and

100 debentures at 1000 FRS each.

questions.enonce_markdown:
How much capital will the company raise through the sale of all these securities?

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** The capital raised is the sum of the money received from each type of security: the **number of securities sold multiplied by the price of one**. (The question paper writes the currency as "FRS"; it is the FCFA used in Cameroon.)

**Step 1: Preference shares.**

$$\text{Preference shares} = 200 \times 5\,000 = 1\,000\,000 \text{ FRS}$$

**Step 2: Ordinary shares.**

$$\text{Ordinary shares} = 400 \times 10\,000 = 4\,000\,000 \text{ FRS}$$

**Step 3: Debentures.**

$$\text{Debentures} = 100 \times 1\,000 = 100\,000 \text{ FRS}$$

**Step 4: Total capital raised.**

$$\text{Total} = 1\,000\,000 + 4\,000\,000 + 100\,000 = 5\,100\,000 \text{ FRS}$$

| Security | Number | Price per unit (FRS) | Amount raised (FRS) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Preference shares | 200 | 5 000 | 1 000 000 |
| Ordinary shares | 400 | 10 000 | 4 000 000 |
| Debentures | 100 | 1 000 | 100 000 |
| **Total** | | | **5 100 000** |

**Conclusion.** Lifeless Ltd will raise **5 100 000 FRS** (of which 5 000 000 FRS is share capital and 100 000 FRS is loan capital from debenture holders).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain Two (2) weaknesses of this kind of business structure.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Lifeless Ltd is a **private limited company** owned by one family, which sells shares and debentures to a small group of members. The structure has the following weaknesses.

1. **Limited ability to raise capital.** Its shares cannot be offered to the general public or sold on the stock exchange, and the number of members is small. The firm can therefore raise only a limited amount of money from the family and its friends, which restricts its expansion.

2. **Difficulty of transferring shares, and family control.** A member who wants to leave cannot freely sell his shares: the other members must usually agree, and it may be hard to find a buyer. Decisions are in the hands of one family, so quarrels within the family, or the death of a member, can disturb the business and reduce its efficiency.

(Other correct points: members' liability is limited, so creditors may be reluctant to lend without security; the company must keep accounts and follow legal formalities, which costs money; and there is little outside pressure or expertise in management.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Differentiate between an ordinary shareholder and debenture holder.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Ordinary shares and debentures are both ways in which a company raises money, but they give the holders very different positions in the company.

| | Ordinary shareholder | Debenture holder |
|---|---|---|
| Position in the company | An **owner** of the company: he holds part of its share capital. | A **creditor** of the company: he has **lent money** to it (loan capital). |
| Return | Receives a **dividend** that varies with the profit of the company. It may be high or nothing at all. | Receives a **fixed rate of interest** every year, whether or not the company makes a profit. |
| Payment order | Paid **after** all debts, interest and preference dividends have been paid. | Paid **before** the shareholders; the interest is an expense of the company. |
| Risk | **High risk**: he is the first to lose when the company does badly and the last to be paid if it closes down. | **Lower risk**: the loan is often secured on the assets of the company and is repaid first. |
| Voting rights | Has the **right to vote** at the general meeting and so takes part in electing the directors. | **No voting rights**, because he is not an owner. |
| Repayment | The money is **not repaid** by the company during its life; the holder can only sell his shares. | The loan is **repaid at a fixed date** (the redemption date). |
| Gain from success | Shares in the profit and may gain from a rise in the value of the shares. | Gains nothing more than the fixed interest. |

**Conclusion.** The ordinary shareholder is the owner and takes the greater risk for a possibly higher reward and a say in the company, while the debenture holder is a lender who has a safe, fixed return and no control.
